ow10_firms.topic: Israeli spyware and security firms in the US: NSO, Paragon, Cellebrite, Elbit/Twenty-Six Defense, Cognyte, Black Cube, Carbyne

claims.text: FBI bought Pegasus (NYT Magazine: 2019; NYT FOIA documents: first purchase 2018), paid NSO about $5m, tested it two years at a New Jersey facility, also tested Phantom for US numbers; pushed to use it late 2020–mid 2021; on 22 Jul 2021 decided to 'cease all efforts'; FBI: 'no operational use'
NYT 2023: US contractor Riva Networks used NSO's Landmark geolocation tool for the FBI after the Nov 2021 ban; FBI says it was misled; Wray terminated the contract; White House said it was unaware

Commerce added NSO and Candiru to Entity List 3 Nov 2021 for supplying spyware used to 'maliciously target government officials, journalists, businesspeople, activists, academics, and embassy workers'

At least nine State Department employees' iPhones (based in or focused on Uganda) hacked with NSO tools (Reuters, Dec 2021); NSO cancelled customer access; Israeli embassy: spyware licensed only for counter-terror and serious crime
Israel's MOD approves countries to which cyber firms may sell; in Nov 2021 cut the list from 102 to 37; NSO said it sold only to MOD-approved countries
WhatsApp v NSO: jury 6 May 2025 awarded $444,719 compensatory and $167.25m punitive for hacking about 1,400 users
Judge Phyllis Hamilton (Oct 2025) cut punitive damages to $4m and issued permanent injunction barring NSO from targeting WhatsApp users
June 2026 WhatsApp alleged NSO violated the injunction and filed for contempt; NSO appeal pending at Ninth Circuit
Apple moved to drop its NSO suit 13 Sep 2024, citing threat-intelligence exposure and a Guardian report that Israeli officials seized NSO files
NSO reportedly owned by investors led by Robert Simonds; David Friedman named executive chairman Nov 2025; founders no longer hold stake; Friedman focused on US government business
EO 14093 (27 Mar 2023) bars operational use of commercial spyware posing counterintelligence risks or risks of improper use by foreign governments; waiver up to one year
AE Industrial Partners agreed to buy Paragon (Dec 2024) for an estimated $900m, merging it into REDLattice; founders include Ehud Schneorson; Ehud Barak reportedly holds several percent (~$10–15m)
Israeli MOD said (19 Dec 2024) the Paragon sale had not yet received the required approval; transfers to foreign hands require a special licence
ICE contract 70CTD024P00000012 with Paragon, $2m, summary signed 27 Sep 2024; hold placed in Oct 2024; modification lifting it reported 1 Sep 2025

Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons, letter of 1 Apr 2026, said HSI uses the tool against groups 'particularly those involved in the trafficking of fentanyl', certified no significant counterintelligence risk under EO 14093

WhatsApp said about 90 journalists and civil society members targeted by Graphite (early 2025); Citizen Lab confirmed infections incl. Ciro Pellegrino; COPASIR confirmed Italian government use; Paragon ended Italian contract (disputed by DIS)
Cellebrite: founded 1999 Petah Tikva; Sun Corporation (Japan) largest shareholder ~44%; Nasdaq via SPAC Aug 2021; ICE contracts ~$2.2m 2017, $30–35m 2019, $11m 2025
ICE $11m Cellebrite contract Sept 2025 with justification fully redacted; CBP, NCIS and Marine CID also use Cellebrite
ICE C3 procurement: 'no other mobile forensic product suites that offer equivalent capabilities'
Citizen Lab (Jan 2026): Jordan used Cellebrite UFED on phones of activists seized at Gaza war protests; Cellebrite does 'not comment on specifics'
Cellebrite halted sales to Russian and Belarusian state bodies in March 2021
Elbit US subsidiary won $145m DHS/CBP Integrated Fixed Tower contract, 2014, Arizona
Elbit America rebranded Twenty-Six Defense 8 Sep 2026; Fort Worth; ~3,300 employees; July 2026 CBP contracts worth more than $370m through May 2029

Cognyte, spun off from Verint Feb 2021, won Myanmar MPT intercept tender before 2021 coup (Reuters); Meta banned Cognyte in 2021; Israel says defence exports to Myanmar banned since 2017; MOD declined comment
Black Cube hired for Weinstein; agents posing as wealth advisers approached Rose McGowan (New Yorker, Nov 2017)

New Yorker 2018: Black Cube directed in May 2017 to dig into Ben Rhodes and Colin Kahl; Black Cube denied relation to Trump administration; describes itself as veterans of Israeli elite intelligence units; Boies retained it in 2016
Barak formed Sum (E.B.) 2015 LP to invest in Reporty/Carbyne; Haaretz: much of the money from Epstein; Barak called Epstein-linked firm a passive investor and asked lawyers to remove it
Kan: Epstein put $1m into Sum in 2016 via Southern Trust; Barak invested $1m 2015 and chaired Carbyne; Founders Fund among backers
Carbyne HQ moved to New York 2019; used in 23 US states; Barak left board 2020; Axon acquisition closed 18 Feb 2026
Axon agreed 6 Nov 2025 to acquire Carbyne for $625m
Globes 30 Jan 2025: Paragon sale to AE Industrial closed in December 2024 with ~$500m cash paid before Defense Ministry formal approval.
